name: Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge
story: The Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge covers 402,000 acres in Georgia and Florida, United States. It protects the Okefenokee Swamp, a shallow, peat-filled wetland formed over the past 6,500 years. The vast bog features open wet prairies, cypress forests, and numerous lakes.
matters: The swamp is one of the world's largest intact freshwater wetland ecosystems and is world-renowned for its amphibian populations that serve as bio-indicators of global health.
